root_cause.text: x86 kexec code calls `load_segments()` and then continues executing KCOV-instrumented C code even though `load_segments()` invalidates the GS base used for KCOV per-CPU state, causing subsequent KCOV fast-path accesses to crash the kernel.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that `load_segments()` “changes segment registers, invalidating GS base (which KCOV relies on for per-cpu data)” and that “any subsequent instrumented C code call (e.g. native_gdt_invalidate()) begins crashing the kernel in an endless loop”; the patch fixes this by disabling KCOV instrumentation for `machine_kexec_64.o` and `physaddr.o` in the Makefiles.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for machine_kexec_64.o to prevent kexec-related crashes caused by KCOV's reliance on GS base per-CPU data.
intent_record.what: The Makefile adds a comment block explaining a KCOV/kexec incompatibility and introduces `KCOV_INSTRUMENT_machine_kexec_64.o := n` to disable KCOV instrumentation for the entire `machine_kexec_64.o` object file.
intent_record.how: At runtime, code in `machine_kexec_64.o` will no longer be instrumented by KCOV, avoiding the crash scenario caused by `load_segments()` invalidating the GS base that KCOV uses for per-CPU data during kexec. This preserves kexec operation while sacrificing coverage collection for that object.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable KCOV instrumentation for physaddr.o to keep it out of coverage instrumentation.
intent_record.what: A new KCOV_INSTRUMENT exclusion was added for physaddr.o, with a comment pointing to the "Disable KCOV" note in arch/x86/kernel/Makefile.
intent_record.how: This prevents KCOV instrumentation from being applied to physaddr.o during the build, avoiding coverage instrumentation in that object file at runtime.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it disables KCOV instrumentation in machine_kexec_64.o to avoid executing KCOV fast-path code after load_segments() invalidates GS base per-CPU state.

The root cause is a KCOV crash caused by executing instrumented code after GS base is invalidated. Disabling KCOV instrumentation for the affected object directly addresses that issue by preventing KCOV fast-path accesses in this code path.

candidates.rationale: This is part of the existing KCOV instrumentation control for x86 kernel objects in the same area as the affected kexec code. The vulnerability arises because machine_kexec_64.o remained KCOV-instrumented even though load_segments() breaks GS-based per-CPU state; the relevant vulnerable condition is that KCOV instrumentation was not disabled for the kexec object.

This line shows the pre-fix pattern of selectively disabling KCOV for specific x86 objects. The vulnerable code path is the omission of a similar disable for machine_kexec_64.o, allowing KCOV fast-path accesses after load_segments() invalidated GS base state.

vuln_statements.explanation: This shows the existing KCOV opt-out mechanism in the x86 Makefile. The vulnerability stems from machine_kexec_64.o not being similarly exempted, allowing KCOV-instrumented execution after load_segments() invalidated GS-based per-CPU state.
This is another example of the pre-fix KCOV exclusion pattern in the same area. The missing equivalent exclusion for the kexec object is what left the crash-prone KCOV instrumentation enabled.
